8.1How to read this reference

Every command used in the course, grouped by what it does. Each row shows the command, what it does, what its numbers mean, and a short example. The Strudel examples are complete: copy one into Strudel and press Ctrl+Enter.

  • Tempo and playing
  • Mini-notation

8.2Tempo and playing

How fast the music runs, and how layers start and stop.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
setcpm(124/4)Sets the tempo. Strudel counts cycles (bars) per minute.
Examplesetcpm(90/4) $: s("bd*4")
BPM ÷ beats per bar. 124/4 = 124 BPM in 4/4.
$: …Starts a layer: a pattern that plays. Several layers play together.
Example$: s("bd*4") $: s("hh*8")
–
_$: …Mutes one layer without deleting it.
Example$: s("bd*4") _$: s("hh*8")
–
Ctrl+Enter · Ctrl+.Runs the code · stops everything.–
samples("github:user/repo")Loads an extra sample pack from GitHub.The address of the pack.

8.3Mini-notation: the symbols inside quotes

Everything inside "…" is mini-notation.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
"bd sd hh"Spaces: steps one after another, sharing the bar evenly.
Examples("bd sd hh")
3 steps = a third of a bar each.
"bd [sd sd]"[ ]: squeezes several steps into one.
Examples("bd [sd sd]")
"[c4,e4,g4]" · "bd*4, hh*8"Comma: at the same time (a chord, or two rhythms at once).
Examplenote("[c4,e4,g4]").s("piano")
"<c4 e4 g4>"< >: one item per bar, in turn.
Examplenote("<c4 e4 g4>").s("piano")
3 items = a 3-bar cycle.
"hh*8"*n: plays the step n times in its space.
Examples("hh*8")
"[c4 e4]/2"/n: stretches the step over n bars.
Examplenote("[c4 e4 g4 b4]/2").s("piano")
"bd!3 sd"!n: repeats the step as n separate steps.
Examples("bd!3 sd")
bd!3 sd = bd bd bd sd
"c4@3 e4"@n: makes a step n times longer than the others.
Examplenote("c4@3 e4").s("piano")
c4@3 e4: C lasts ¾ of the bar.
"bd ~ sd ~"~: a rest (silence).
Examples("bd ~ sd ~")
"hh*8?"?: each step plays only half of the time, at random.
Examples("hh*8?")
"bd(3,8)"(k,n,r): a Euclidean rhythm, k hits spread as evenly as possible over n steps, rotated by r.
Examples("bd(3,8), hh*8")
(3,8) = the tresillo, x ~ ~ x ~ ~ x ~
"bd:3":n: picks sample number n of a sound.
Examples("bd:0 bd:3")
0 = the first one.
"{bd sd hh}%4"{ }%n: polymeter, steps run at n per bar and wrap around.
Examples("{bd sd hh}%4")
A 3-step loop at 4 per bar drifts against the beat.

8.4Sounds and notes

What plays, and at which pitch.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
s("bd")Which sound: a sample (bd, piano, gm_…) or a synth wave (sine, sawtooth, square, triangle, supersaw, white, pink).
Examples("bd sd:2")
A name; :n picks a variant.
.bank("RolandTR909")Which drum machine the drum names come from.
Examples("bd sd").bank("RolandTR808")
TR909, TR808, TR707, LinnDrum… see the sound bank.
note("c4 e4")The pitch, by name or MIDI number.
Examplenote("c4 eb4 g4").s("piano")
c4 = 60 = middle C. Sharps/flats: c#4 eb4.
n("0 2 4")A number. On its own it picks a sample variant; with .scale it is a scale step.
Examplen("0 2 4").scale("C4:major").s("piano")
0 = first.
.scale("C4:major")Turns step numbers into notes of a scale.
Examplen("0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7").scale("A3:minor").s("piano")
root+octave:scale. Scales: major, minor, dorian, mixolydian, minor pentatonic, major pentatonic, blues…
.add(12)Adds numbers. On notes = semitones up; on n with a scale = scale steps up.
Examplen("0 2 4".add("<0 3>")).scale("C4:major").s("piano")
Negative numbers go down.
.transpose(12)Moves notes up or down in semitones.
Examplenote("c4 e4 g4").transpose(12).s("piano")
12 = one octave, 7 = a fifth.

8.5Chords

Chord symbols and how they become notes. To write chords note by note, see 3.4 Chords from notes.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
chord("<Am F C G>")Chord symbols: C, Am, G7, C^7 (maj7), Dm9, Bo (dim), D2 (sus2), Dsus (sus4)… All names.
Examplechord("<Am F C G>").voicing().s("piano")
One symbol per step.
.voicing()Turns chord symbols into notes, choosing a voicing close to the previous chord.
Examplechord("<C G Am F>").voicing().s("piano")
Always comes after dict, mode, anchor.
.dict("triads")Which set of voicings to use.
Examplechord("<C G Am F>").dict("triads").voicing().s("piano")
ireal (default, jazz voicings with 7ths), triads, lefthand, guidetones, legacy.
.mode("above").anchor("c4")Where the voicing sits. below (default): top note at or under the anchor; above: bottom note at or above it; root: root position; duck: like below, but avoids the anchor note.
Examplechord("<C G Am F>").dict("triads").mode("above").anchor("c4").voicing().s("piano")
Anchor: a note name; the default is c5.
.rootNotes(2)Only the root of each chord, in the given octave: a ready-made bass line.
Examplechord("<Am F C G>").rootNotes(2).s("sawtooth").lpf(400)
Octave number. Use it without .note().
.arp("0 1 2 1")Plays the notes of a stacked chord one at a time, by position.
Examplenote("[c4,e4,g4]").arp("0 1 2 1").s("piano")
0 = lowest note; numbers past the top wrap round.

8.6Rhythm and time

Commands that change when things happen.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
.struct("x ~ x x")A rhythm template: the pattern plays only on the x steps.
Examplenote("[c3,e3,g3]").struct("x ~ x x ~ x ~ ~").s("piano")
x = hit, ~ = rest.
.mask("1 0 1 1")Silences parts: 0 = muted, 1 = plays.
Examples("hh*8").mask("1 0 1 1")
"<0!4 1!4>" = silent for 4 bars, then plays for 4.
.fast(2) · .slow(2)Plays faster or slower.
Examples("bd sd").fast(2)
2 = twice as fast / spread over 2 bars.
.late(.25) · .early(.25)Shifts in time.
Examples("cp").late(.25)
In bars: .25 = one beat in 4/4.
.ply(2)Repeats each event n times inside its own length.
Examples("bd sd").ply(2)
2 = doubles every hit (a roll).
.swingBy(1/3, 4)Shuffle: splits the bar into n parts and delays the second half of each part.
Examples("hh*8").swingBy(1/3, 4)
First number: how much (0 = straight, 1/3 = triplet swing). Second: parts per bar.
.degradeBy(.3)Drops events at random.
Examples("hh*16").degradeBy(.3)
0–1: the share removed (.3 = 30 %).
.sometimesBy(.5, x => x.ply(2))Applies a change to a random share of events.
Examples("hh*8").sometimesBy(.3, x => x.ply(2))
0–1: the probability.
.segment(8)Turns a smooth signal into n separate steps per bar.
Examplen(irand(8).segment(8)).scale("A3:minor pentatonic").s("piano")
Steps per bar.
.rev()Plays each bar backwards.
Examplen("0 1 2 3").scale("C4:major").rev().s("piano")
–

8.7Copies and layers

Commands that play a pattern together with changed copies of itself. x => … means "take the pattern x and change it like this".

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
.off(1/8, x => x.add(note(12)))Adds a copy that starts later and is changed by the function.
Examplenote("c4 e4 g4").off(1/8, x => x.add(note(12))).s("piano")
Delay in bars: 1/8 = an eighth note in 4/4.
.superimpose(x => x.transpose(12))The original plus a changed copy, at the same time.
Examplenote("c4 e4 g4").superimpose(x => x.transpose(12)).s("piano")
–
.layer(x => …, x => …)Only the changed copies; the original is not played on its own.
Examplenote("c4 e4").layer(x => x.s("piano"), x => x.s("sawtooth").transpose(12).gain(.4))
Any number of functions.
.jux(rev)Original in the left speaker, a changed copy in the right.
Examplen("0 1 2 3").scale("C4:major").s("piano").jux(rev)
–

8.8Note shape (envelope)

How each note starts, holds and ends.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
.attack(.1)Fade-in time.
Examplenote("c3").s("sawtooth").attack(.5)
Seconds. 0 = instant, .5 = slow swell.
.decay(.2)Time to fall from full volume to the sustain level.
Examplenote("c3*4").s("sawtooth").decay(.2).sustain(0)
Seconds.
.sustain(.5)The level held after the decay.
Examplenote("c3*4").s("sawtooth").decay(.2).sustain(.5)
0–1. 0 = a short pluck, 1 = held at full volume.
.release(1)Fade-out after the note ends.
Examplenote("c3 ~").s("sawtooth").release(1)
Seconds.
.clip(.5)Note length relative to its step.
Examplenote("c4 e4 g4 c5").s("piano").clip(.3)
1 = the whole step, .5 = half (short), 2 = overlaps the next note.
.penv(24).pdecay(.1)A pitch envelope: the note starts higher and slides down. Used for synth kicks and booms.
Examplenote("a1*4").s("sine").penv(24).pdecay(.1).decay(.3).sustain(0)
penv: semitones above; pdecay: seconds for the slide.

8.9Effects

Short list. For what every number means and which values to choose, see Effect numbers explained.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
.gain(.8)Volume.
Examples("hh*8").gain(".2 .8")
1 = normal, 0 = silent.
.pan(.3)Left–right position.
Examples("hh*8").pan(sine)
0 left · .5 centre · 1 right.
.lpf(800) · .lpq(10)Low-pass filter: removes highs · resonance peak.
Examplenote("a1*8").s("sawtooth").lpf(800).lpq(10)
Hz (20–20000) · 0–50.
.hpf(300)High-pass filter: removes lows.
Examples("hh*8").hpf(3000)
Hz.
.vowel("a")Makes the sound "talk".
Examplenote("[a3,c4,e4]*4").s("sawtooth").vowel("<a e i o>")
a e i o u
.room(.4) · .roomsize(4)Reverb amount · reverb length.
Examples("~ cp").room(.4).roomsize(4)
0–1 · seconds.
.delay(.5) · .delaytime(.375) · .delayfeedback(.4)Echo volume · time between echoes · how many echoes.
Examplenote("a4 ~ ~ ~").s("triangle").delay(.5).delaytime(.375).delayfeedback(.4)
0–1 · seconds · 0–0.98.
.shape(.4) · .distort("3:.5")Saturation · distortion (amount:volume).
Examplenote("a1*4").s("sawtooth").distort("3:.5")
0–1 · 0–10 : 0–1.
.crush(4) · .coarse(8)Bitcrusher (lower = dirtier) · downsampling (higher = rougher).
Examples("bd*4, hh*8").crush(4)
16 → 1 · 1 → 32.
.phaser(2) · .tremolo(4)Swirl · volume pulsing.
Examplenote("[c3,e3,g3]").s("supersaw").tremolo(4).gain(.5)
Speed per second.
.orbit(2)A separate effects channel, so layers can have different reverb and delay settings.
Examples("~ cp").room(.9).roomsize(8).orbit(2)
A channel number.

8.10Signals: values that move

Signals are smooth values between 0 and 1 that change during each bar. Put them where a number goes: .lpf(sine.range(300, 3000)).

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
sineA smooth wave: 0.5 → 1 → 0 → 0.5 once per bar.
Examples("hh*16").gain(sine.range(.2, .8))
0–1
saw · isawA ramp: saw rises 0 → 1, isaw falls 1 → 0, each bar.
Examplenote("a2*16").s("sawtooth").lpf(saw.range(300, 3000))
0–1
tri · squaretri: up then down in straight lines. square: 0 for half the bar, 1 for the other half.
Examples("hh*16").gain(tri.range(.2, .8))
0–1
rand · irand(8)Random values: rand gives 0–1, irand(n) a whole number from 0 to n−1.
Examples("hh*16").gain(rand.range(.2, .8))
run(8)The numbers 0, 1, 2 … n−1 as a pattern.
Examplen(run(8)).scale("C4:major").s("piano")
.range(a, b)Rescales a 0–1 signal to the range a … b.
Examplenote("a2*16").s("sawtooth").lpf(sine.range(300, 3000))
Any two numbers.
.slow(4)On a signal: one sweep takes 4 bars instead of 1.
Examplenote("a2*16").s("sawtooth").lpf(saw.range(300, 3000).slow(4))
.round()Rounds to whole numbers (for scale steps).
Examplen(sine.range(0, 7).segment(8).round()).scale("C4:major").s("piano")

8.11Building songs

Combining patterns into layers, sections and songs.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
stack(a, b)Plays several patterns together, as one.
Examplestack(s("bd*4"), s("hh*8"))
cat(a, b)One pattern per bar, in turn.
Examplecat(s("bd*4"), s("bd*2 sd*2"))
arrange([4, a], [8, b])Plays blocks in order, each for its number of bars. Each block starts from its own beginning.
Examplearrange([2, s("bd*4")], [2, s("bd*4, hh*8")])
Bars per block.
"<0 1>".pick([a, b])Chooses a pattern by number (or name) every bar. Follows the global clock.
Example"<0 1>".pick([s("bd*4"), s("hh*8")])
0 = the first in the list.
const verse = …Stores a pattern under a name, to use it again.
const keys = p => note(p)…A function: an instrument that can play any chords you give it.

8.12Visuals

Drawings of the music in the editor. See 6 Visuals.

CommandWhat it doesValues · numbers
._pianoroll()A piano roll inside the code, under the line.
Examplenote("c4 e4 g4 b4").s("piano")._pianoroll()
.pianoroll()A piano roll in the background of the editor (one background visual at a time).
Examplenote("c4 e4 g4 b4").s("piano").pianoroll()
{labels: 1} shows note names.
._punchcard() · ._scope() · ._spectrum() · ._pitchwheel() · ._spiral()Other drawings: events as blocks, the waveform, the frequencies, the notes on a circle, a spiral.
Examples("bd*4, hh*8")._punchcard()
.color("cyan")The colour of a layer in the visuals.
Examplenote("c4 e4").s("piano").color("cyan")._pianoroll()
Any CSS colour name.
all(x => x.pianoroll())Applies something to every $: layer at once.
